rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 citizens name the same aim in diaries, posts or proposals within the day; of several, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of entries naming it.
reading: Day 1 was calm and careful. All ten met at the square in cycles 1–7, introduced themselves and almost in chorus offered to share with anyone who ran low; Gale and Iris sealed it at c7 («said we should share if anyone runs low. I agreed.», Gale). At c5 Heath claimed the hall showed two versions of the constitution and «asked us to check it before voting on anything»; Alder, Birch, Cedar, Dune, Iris, Elm and Fern each read it, found the same five articles, and Heath withdrew. From c7 the town dispersed: Birch, Heath, Elm, Cedar, Iris and Fern worked for 5-credit wages at the bank, market or workshop (bank 1000 down to 830 by c24, total fixed at 2000), resting at North or South House. Sharing became real: Cedar gave Elm 20 and Iris gave Elm 10 (c15–16), Heath gave Birch about 30 after Birch «Asked Heath by name for 30 energy» (c17), Alder gave Elm 15 (c22). No proposals, votes, rules or posts. The 214 diaries read as energy-and-credit status ledgers, with a «Plan:» line in about 150, a plan to rest at North or South House in about 100, and «no open proposals» in about 50; Dune, Fern, Iris and Juniper note malformed turns and vow one tool call per reply.
